history.heading: Silk Road oases
paragraphs: Turkmenistan, in Central Asia, is mostly covered by the Karakum Desert. Ancient civilisations flourished in its oases: Gonur Tepe was a Bronze Age centre, and Merv, an important Silk Road city, was one of the largest cities in the world in the 12th century under the Seljuks before its destruction by the Mongols in 1221. Nisa was a capital of the Parthian Empire.
Turkmen tribes, descended from the Oghuz Turks, lived as nomadic herders and were famed horse breeders, raising the Akhal-Teke horse.

history.heading: Russian and Soviet rule
paragraphs: The Russian Empire conquered the region in the 1880s after fierce resistance, including the siege of Geok Tepe in 1881. The Turkmen SSR was created in 1924. Soviet irrigation, including the Karakum Canal, expanded cotton production but contributed to the drying of the Aral Sea.

Turkmenistan became independent on 27 October 1991. Saparmurat Niyazov, who called himself Turkmenbashi ("Father of the Turkmen"), built an extreme personality cult, renaming months after himself and his mother. Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow succeeded him in 2006, and his son Serdar became president in 2022.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Turkmen, a Turkic language written in Latin script, is the official language; Russian is also spoken. Most people are Sunni Muslim. Hand-woven carpets, featured on the flag, and Akhal-Teke horses are national symbols. The Darvaza gas crater, called the "Door to Hell", has burned for decades. Plov and dograma are traditional dishes.

politics.heading: Authoritarian state
paragraphs: Turkmenistan is one of the most closed and repressive countries in the world. Power is held by the Berdimuhamedow family; the former president remains highly influential as head of the upper house of parliament. There is no real opposition or independent media, and internet access is heavily restricted. The country follows a policy of "permanent neutrality" recognised by the UN.

economy.heading: Gas wealth
paragraphs: Turkmenistan has the world's fourth-largest natural gas reserves, and gas exports, mainly to China via pipeline, dominate the economy. Cotton is also important, produced with forced labour according to human rights groups. The state controls most of the economy, and the capital, Ashgabat, is known for its white marble buildings. The currency is the manat.
